issues.legal_issue: The value of land with a building may be assessed by separately valuing the land and the depreciated building when that method is appropriate to the property and relevant factors are considered.
material_facts: The partition proceeding concerned land and a two-storeyed building that the parties accepted could not be divided by metes and bounds.
A valuer assessed the current market value by adding the land value to the depreciated value of the building, taking relevant features of the property into account.
A co-owner challenged that method and argued that the property should instead be valued as a single unit by capitalizing rental value.
The property had been renovated and extended, and the Court accepted the valuation made by the valuer.
issues.conclusion: The Court accepted the valuation based on the land value and the depreciated value of the building, holding that capitalization of rental value is not the only permissible method of valuation.
issues.legal_principle: In a partition proceeding involving land with a building, the method of valuation depends on the circumstances; capitalization of actual or reasonably obtainable rent is not the only method. The Court distinguished State of Kerala v. P.P. Hassan Koya, which concerned compensation under the Land Acquisition Act and did not establish a universal valuation method.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and indivisible_land_and_building and current_component_valuation and relevant_property_factors_considered

predicates.partition_proceeding: The case is a proceeding to partition property among co-owners.
predicates.indivisible_land_and_building: The property consists of land and a building that cannot be divided by metes and bounds.
predicates.current_component_valuation: A valuer assesses the current value of the land and the depreciated value of the building separately.
predicates.relevant_property_factors_considered: The valuer takes relevant features of the property into account when assessing its value.

issues.definition: When an indivisible property comprising land and a building is valued currently by assessing its components and considering relevant property factors, separate component valuation may be accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A co-owner who sought to purchase the other co-owners' shares at a valuation cannot then insist on an auction to establish the property's market value after opposing an order for an auction.
material_facts: The proceeding concerned partition of property that could not be divided by metes and bounds.
A co-owner applied to purchase the other parties' shares at a valuation.
That co-owner opposed an order directing a public auction and appealed against it, but later argued that an auction should determine the market value.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the co-owner's contention that the property should be auctioned, finding that the contention was inconsistent with the co-owner's earlier application and conduct.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2 and 3 of the Partition Act, 1893 provide for sale of property and purchase of other shares by a co-owner, respectively. A party who sought to buy the other shares at a valuation and opposed an auction order cannot take the inconsistent position that an auction must be held; the Court described that position as blowing hot and cold.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and indivisible_property and coowner_applied_to_buy_shares_at_valuation and coowner_opposed_auction_order and coowner_later_advocated_auction

predicates.partition_proceeding: The case is a proceeding to partition property among co-owners.
predicates.indivisible_property: The property cannot be divided by metes and bounds.
predicates.coowner_applied_to_buy_shares_at_valuati: A co-owner applied to purchase the other co-owners' shares at a valuation.
predicates.coowner_opposed_auction_order: The co-owner opposed or appealed an order directing an auction of the property.
predicates.coowner_later_advocated_auction: The co-owner later argued that an auction should be used to establish the property's market value.

issues.definition: If a co-owner in an indivisible-property partition proceeding applied to buy the other shares at a valuation, opposed an auction order, and later advocated an auction, the later auction contention is rejected as inconsistent.

issues.legal_issue: Where co-owners offer to purchase one another's shares at an accepted valuation, the Court may provide for a first purchase opportunity and a fallback purchase if the first purchaser does not complete the purchase.
material_facts: The partition proceeding concerned property that could not be divided by metes and bounds.
The Court accepted a current valuation of the property.
One co-owner remained willing to purchase the other parties' shares at that valuation.
The other co-owners undertook to purchase the competing co-owners' shares at a different valuation if the first co-owner did not complete the purchase.

The Court directed that the first co-owner could acquire the shares by depositing the purchase amount within the specified period and that, on default, the other co-owners could acquire the shares by making their own deposit within the specified period.
issues.conclusion: The Court ordered a sequential purchase arrangement: the co-owner who remained willing to buy could purchase the other shares at the accepted valuation, and if that purchase was not completed, the other co-owners could purchase the remaining shares on the terms of their undertaking.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Partition Act, 1893 provides for a co-owner to seek purchase of the shares of the other parties at a valuation. In disposing of the partition appeal, the Court applied the accepted valuation and the parties' purchase offers and undertakings to frame a conditional order for allotment; no earlier case was relied on for this specific arrangement.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and indivisible_property and accepted_valuation and first_coowner_willing_to_buy and fallback_coowners_undertook_to_buy and first_purchase_not_completed

predicates.partition_proceeding: The case is a proceeding to partition property among co-owners.
predicates.indivisible_property: The property cannot be divided by metes and bounds.
predicates.accepted_valuation: The Court accepts a valuation of the property for the proposed purchase of shares.
predicates.first_coowner_willing_to_buy: A co-owner remains willing to purchase the other co-owners' shares at the accepted valuation.
predicates.fallback_coowners_undertook_to_buy: Other co-owners undertake to purchase the competing co-owners' shares if the first proposed purchase is not completed.
predicates.first_purchase_not_completed: The first proposed purchaser does not complete the purchase as directed.

issues.definition: If an indivisible-property partition proceeding has an accepted valuation, a willing first purchaser, and other co-owners who have undertaken to buy if that purchase fails, failure to complete the first purchase gives the fallback purchasers an opportunity to acquire the shares.
